sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐秘”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: There's a storefront at a major intersection in downtown Toronto, at Spadina and King Street.
sentences.zh: 多伦多市中心有一个主要路口，在斯帕迪纳街和金街交汇处，那里有一家临街店面。

sentences.en: The space is about 11,000 square feet, and it used to house a massive liquor store right in the middle of Canada's biggest city.
sentences.zh: 这个空间大约有11000平方英尺，过去是一家大型烈酒商店，就开在加拿大最大城市的正中心。

sentences.en: For years, I worked down the street, and let me tell you, that liquor store was bumpin'.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我一直在街那头工作，说实话，那家烈酒商店生意火爆得很。

sentences.en: That's producer Chris Berube.
sentences.zh: 那是制作人克里斯·贝鲁比。

sentences.en: I remember lines out the door before holidays, and setting aside a whole lunch hour just to get a bottle of wine.
sentences.zh: 我记得节日前排队都排到了门外，甚至要特地腾出整个午休时间去买瓶红酒。

sentences.en: But in 2019, the liquor store moved to a new, bigger location close by, and the shop at Spadina and King closed.
sentences.zh: 但在2019年，这家烈酒商店搬到了附近一个更大、更新的地点，斯帕迪纳与金街交汇处的这家店便关门了。

sentences.en: Since then, all 11,000 square feet have been empty.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，这整整11000平方英尺的空间就一直空着。

sentences.en: For a long time, I wondered, okay, what is going to move in there?
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，我都在琢磨：好吧，到底什么店会搬进这里呢？

sentences.en: I mean, this is a big-time space right downtown.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可是市中心黄金地段的大面积空间。

sentences.en: But in 2019, it sat empty.
sentences.zh: 但在2019年，它闲置着。

sentences.en: 2020, still empty.
sentences.zh: 2020年，依然空置。

sentences.en: 2021, empty.
sentences.zh: 2021年，空空如也。

sentences.en: 2022, okay, you get the point.
sentences.zh: 2022年……好吧，你懂我意思了。

sentences.en: But it's only empty for about nine months out of the year.
sentences.zh: 但它一年中其实只空置大约九个月。

sentences.en: Because every fall, just like clockwork, the space has been possessed by a spirit.
sentences.zh: 因为每年秋天，就像钟表一样准时，这个空间会被一个幽灵附体。

sentences.en: By spirit Halloween.
sentences.zh: 一个万圣节幽灵。

sentences.en: If you live in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果你住在美国或加拿大，

sentences.en: or Canada, you have probably seen the orange, yellow, and black spirit Halloween signs.
sentences.zh: 你很可能见过那种橙色、黄色和黑色的“万圣节幽灵”招牌。

sentences.en: They go up sometime in August in 1,500 empty storefronts.
sentences.zh: 它们通常在8月某时候挂出来，出现在1500家空置的店铺里。

sentences.en: And by early November, all of them disappear.
sentences.zh: 而到了11月上旬，它们便消失得无影无踪。

sentences.en: Spirit Halloween has become something of an institution.
sentences.zh: “万圣节幽灵”已经变成了一种类似标志性的存在。

sentences.en: If you aren't familiar, I mean, it's pretty simple.
sentences.zh: 如果你不太熟悉，其实很简单。

sentences.en: It's a pop-up store full of Halloween stuff.
sentences.zh: 它是一家摆满万圣节商品的快闪店。

sentences.en: They sell Halloween masks, Halloween costumes, Halloween costumes for dogs, Halloween decorations, creepy robots, and several different kinds of fake blood.
sentences.zh: 他们出售万圣节面具、万圣节服装、狗狗穿的万圣节服装、万圣节装饰品、毛骨悚然的机器人，以及好几种不同的假血浆。

sentences.en: And it's successful.
sentences.zh: 而且它非常成功。

sentences.en: Spirit reportedly sells about a billion dollars worth of merchandise every year.
sentences.zh: 据报道，“万圣节幽灵”每年的商品销售额高达约十亿美元。

sentences.en: For a long time, I resisted going to Spirit because, I don't know, it just seemed like a lot of loud noises and crowds and children running around.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，我都拒绝去“万圣节幽灵”逛，因为我不知道，那感觉就像会有很多刺耳的噪音、拥挤的人群和跑来跑去的小孩。

sentences.en: And I gotta say, when I finally took the plunge last fall, it was pretty much that.
sentences.zh: 我得承认，去年秋天当我终于下定决心去体验时，差不多也就是那么回事。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm passing through a crypt.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我正穿过一个地穴。

sentences.en: Looks like it's set up to look like a crypt.
sentences.zh: 看起来这里被布置得像个地穴一样。

sentences.en: It's just full of those electric candles that kind of look like fire.
sentences.zh: 里面到处都是那种看起来有点像火焰的电动蜡烛。

sentences.en: After passing through rows of plastic gravestones and being yelled at by a terrifying animatronic clown,
sentences.zh: 在穿过一排排塑料墓碑、被一个可怕的电子动画小丑大声吓唬之后，

sentences.en: I discovered this one blue jumpsuit costume that severely creeped me out.
sentences.zh: 我发现了这套让我感到极度毛骨悚然的蓝色连体裤服装。

sentences.en: So I see an avatar one, which honestly is very disturbing.
sentences.zh: 所以，我看到了一个《阿凡达》款式的服装，老实说，这非常让人不安。

sentences.en: I can't imagine dressing a child like this.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象把小孩子打扮成这样。

sentences.en: I don't like it.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢它。

sentences.en: Overall, I'd say the experience wasn't really for me.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我觉得这种体验其实并不适合我。

sentences.en: But I know that my opinion is in the minority here.
sentences.zh: 但我知道，在这里我的看法只是少数。

sentences.en: Because there are a ton of people who are obsessed with Spirit Halloween.
sentences.zh: 因为有大批的人对“万圣节幽灵”着迷不已。

sentences.en: Today is a very special day, my friends.
sentences.zh: 今天是极其特殊的一天，我的朋友们。

sentences.en: Because today is the day that my local Spirit Halloween store has opened.
sentences.zh: 因为今天是我本地的“万圣节幽灵”商店开业的日子。

sentences.en: And we are here right in front of it, about to go in.
sentences.zh: 我们现在就站在它门前，准备进去了。

sentences.en: I'm going to give you a full tour of this year's theme, animatronic.
sentences.zh: 我将带大家完整参观今年以电子动画为主题的店铺。

sentences.en: There are countless YouTube videos from creators who treat the first day of the Spirit calendar like a high holy day.
sentences.zh: YouTube上有无数视频，创作者们把万圣节日历的第一天当作盛大节日来对待。

sentences.en: Walking through the aisles of a freshly opened store and exploring the new products.
sentences.zh: 他们漫步在刚开业的店铺过道里，探索着各种新品。

sentences.en: This guy.
sentences.zh: 这个人。

sentences.en: My name is Jackie.
sentences.zh: 我叫杰基。

sentences.en: And I have a YouTube channel called Super Enthused.
sentences.zh: 我有一个名为“超级狂热”的YouTube频道。

sentences.en: Jackie's videos of Spirit Halloween walkthroughs have garnered hundreds of thousands of views.
sentences.zh: 杰基制作的“万圣节幽灵”探店视频获得了数十万的观看量。

sentences.en: Jackie says the reason Spirit has developed a following is the way they've tried to make the store itself feel like a haunted house.
sentences.zh: 杰基说，“万圣节幽灵”之所以能拥有一批忠实粉丝，是因为他们努力让店铺本身营造出鬼屋的感觉。

sentences.en: One thing I found, like the first thing that hit me was that Spirit kind of let you play with things.
sentences.zh: 我发现的一点，也就是最先冲击到我的地方，是“万圣节幽灵”有点允许你动手把玩各种东西。

sentences.en: They let you stomp on the floor and activate the animatronics and almost all the others.
sentences.zh: 他们让你跺脚来激活那些电子动画装置，几乎所有其他地方都不是这样的。

sentences.en: Especially as like a younger person, a kid, a teenager.
sentences.zh: 特别是对于年轻人、小孩子、青少年来说。

sentences.en: Don't, don't, don't touch.
sentences.zh: 别，别，别碰。

sentences.en: Don't touch that.
sentences.zh: 别碰那个。

sentences.en: Don't open that.
sentences.zh: 别打开那个。

sentences.en: Don't.
sentences.zh: 别动。

sentences.en: You can't touch anything.
sentences.zh: 你什么都不能碰。

sentences.en: You can't play with anything.
sentences.zh: 你什么都不能玩。

sentences.en: They're watching you like a hawk, like if you're going to steal the whole store.
sentences.zh: 他们像鹰一样盯着你，仿佛你打算把整家店偷走似的。

sentences.en: But Spirit's like, come in, touch everything, play with all the things.
sentences.zh: 但“万圣节幽灵”却说：进来吧，什么都摸摸，所有的东西都玩个遍。

sentences.en: Spirit's haunted house energy is a big part of the draw.
sentences.zh: “万圣节幽灵”带来的鬼屋氛围是吸引人的很大一部分原因。

sentences.en: But there's also an element of scarcity.
sentences.zh: 但其中也包含了一种稀缺感。

sentences.en: Because the real hallmark of Spirit Halloween is that it's only open roughly three months out of the year.
sentences.zh: 因为“万圣节幽灵”真正的招牌特色在于，它一年到头只营业大约三个月。

sentences.en: Spirit Halloween has zero permanent year-round locations.
sentences.zh: “万圣节幽灵”没有一家全年开放的永久店面。

sentences.en: And inside these pop-up stores, there's an overwhelming feeling that everything won't be around for long.
sentences.zh: 在这些快闪店里，会有一种挥之不去的强烈感觉：这里的一切都不会持续太久。

sentences.en: The thing that's interesting is that even the walls look temporary.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，甚至连墙壁看起来都是临时的。

sentences.en: Like the walls up here look really thin.
sentences.zh: 就像这里的墙壁看起来非常薄。

sentences.en: They almost look like cardboard walls that have been put up.
sentences.zh: 它们看上去几乎就像是临时搭起来的纸板墙。

sentences.en: Here is what I do not get about Spirit Halloween.
sentences.zh: 这就是我对“万圣节幽灵”最搞不懂的地方。

sentences.en: The last few years have been considered this kind of retail apocalypse,
sentences.zh: 过去几年被认为是零售业的末日，

sentences.en: with lots of brick and mortar chains closing their physical locations.
sentences.zh: 许多实体零售连锁店纷纷关闭了实体店面。

sentences.en: A lot of those retailers have just left empty storefronts across the country.
sentences.zh: 其中许多零售商只在全国各地留下了空置的店面。

sentences.en: So what does it say about the world of retail that a seasonal Halloween store is taking all these abandoned spaces for three months a year and making a killing in the process?
sentences.zh: 那么，一家季节性的万圣节商店一年中有三个月占用所有这些荒废的空间，并在这一过程中大发横财，这说明了零售世界的什么问题呢？

sentences.en: To understand how Spirit became ubiquitous, I called up the guy who started it.
sentences.zh: 为了解“万圣节幽灵”是如何无处不在的，我打电话联系了它的创始人。

sentences.en: Joe Marver opened Spirit in 1983.
sentences.zh: 乔·马尔弗于1983年开了第一家“万圣节幽灵”。

sentences.en: And I'll admit, when I met the father of Spirit Halloween,
sentences.zh: 我得承认，当我见到这位“万圣节幽灵”之父时，

sentences.en: I kind of assumed he'd have a backstory about how he became a Halloween guy.
sentences.zh: 我曾以为他会有一段关于他是如何成为一个“万圣节狂热者”的背景故事。

sentences.en: Like he stumbled into a crypt full of bats.
sentences.zh: 比如他意外闯入了一个满是蝙蝠的地穴。

sentences.en: Or he stumbled upon a pumpkin that was full of bats.
sentences.zh: 或者他偶然发现了一个装满蝙蝠的南瓜。

sentences.en: But it turns out his childhood was disappointingly bat-free.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，他的童年令人失望地与蝙蝠毫无关系。

sentences.en: Did trick-or-treating out of my house.
sentences.zh: 我在自己家里接待过讨糖果的小孩。

sentences.en: I mean, we're going back to 1950s when I was seven years old.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那是20世纪50年代，当时我七岁。

sentences.en: My first costume was Zorro.
sentences.zh: 我的第一套万圣节服装是佐罗。

sentences.en: Okay, but Joe Marver did tell me, as a teen, he attended summer camp at this place with a really spooky name.
sentences.zh: 好吧，不过乔·马尔弗确实告诉我，他青少年时期曾在一个名字听起来非常诡异的地方参加过夏令营。

sentences.en: I went to a camp in Devil's Lake, Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 我去过威斯康星州魔鬼湖的一个营地。

sentences.en: In his 20s, Joe Marver moved west to California in search of his fortune.
sentences.zh: 二十多岁时，乔·马尔弗为了寻找发财的机会，向西搬到了加利福尼亚。

sentences.en: He worked as a clown in Las Vegas, then at a shoe store.
sentences.zh: 他在拉斯维加斯当过小丑，后来又在一家鞋店工作。

sentences.en: And by the early 80s, he owned an outlet store in the Bay Area.
sentences.zh: 到了80年代初，他在湾区拥有一家奥特莱斯店。

sentences.en: A haunted outlet store.
sentences.zh: 一家闹鬼的奥特莱斯店。

sentences.en: It was not haunted.
sentences.zh: 它并没有闹鬼。

sentences.en: It was just a regular store called Spirit Discount Women's Apparel.
sentences.zh: 那只是一家普通的店，名叫“精神折扣女装”。

sentences.en: But right across the parking lot from Joe's store was a dancewear shop.
sentences.zh: 但在乔的店铺停车场马路对面，有一家舞蹈服装店。

sentences.en: They sold leotards and tutus, but also a selection of Halloween costumes.
sentences.zh: 他们出售紧身衣和芭蕾短裙，但也精选了一批万圣节服装。

sentences.en: And watching their customers gave Joe Marver an idea.
sentences.zh: 看着那些顾客，乔·马尔弗萌生了一个主意。

sentences.en: They were lined up around the block for the month of October.
sentences.zh: 在整个十月，他们排队排得拐过街角。

sentences.en: And it was insane because our October stunk in the women's apparel business across the street in a strip center.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了，因为我们在街对面露天购物中心的十月女装生意简直糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: In 1983, the dancewear shop closed.
sentences.zh: 1983年，那家舞蹈服装店关门了。

sentences.en: And Joe Marver decided he could not let those customers go someplace else.
sentences.zh: 乔·马尔弗决定不能让那些顾客去别的地方。

sentences.en: So he put the women's clothing in the basement and bought a crop of Halloween costumes.
sentences.zh: 于是他把女装搬到地下室，并买进了一批万圣节服装。

sentences.en: Hmm, I'm going to go to a trade show.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我要去参加一个贸易展。

sentences.en: I'm going to get wigs, makeup, a lot of products that could be for Halloween.
sentences.zh: 我要买假发、化妆品，以及大量适合万圣节的商品。

sentences.en: That October, Joe completely changed his business for one month only.
sentences.zh: 那个十月，乔彻底改变了他的业务，仅仅维持一个月。

sentences.en: And Spirit Discount Women's Apparel became Spirit Halloween.
sentences.zh: 于是，“精神折扣女装”变成了“万圣节幽灵”。

sentences.en: Our staff totally was dressing up in costume.
sentences.zh: 我们的员工绝对都穿上了化妆服。

sentences.en: Something that might have been a costume that we wanted to sell.
sentences.zh: 那可能是一件我们想要出售的服装。

sentences.en: And it rocked.
sentences.zh: 而且效果好极了。

sentences.en: It was amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: The new business model worked right away.
sentences.zh: 新的商业模式立刻奏效了。

sentences.en: In his second year, Joe says he made $100,000.
sentences.zh: 乔说，在经营的第二年，他赚了10万美元。

sentences.en: Soon, he was running six stores.
sentences.zh: 很快，他经营的店铺达到了六家。

sentences.en: And then even more.
sentences.zh: 然后更多。

sentences.en: And it's from these early stores that we get the not-built-to-last quality
sentences.zh: 正是从这些早期的店铺中，我们体会到了那种“天生不求耐用”的特质，

sentences.en: that's come to define Spirit Halloween.
sentences.zh: 这也成了定义“万圣节幽灵”的标志。

sentences.en: Now, this predates the rise of pop-up retailers.
sentences.zh: 这发生在快闪零售商兴起之前。

sentences.en: Back then, there wasn't this modern concept of
sentences.zh: 在那时，还没有这种现代概念，

sentences.en: a cool artisanal clothing shop that's open for two weeks.
sentences.zh: 比如只开两周的酷炫手工服装店。

sentences.en: Or a food truck in the parking lot of your favorite bar.
sentences.zh: 或者停在你最喜欢的酒吧停车场里的餐车。

sentences.en: Spirit was ahead of all that.
sentences.zh: “万圣节幽灵”走在了所有这些的前面。

sentences.en: And because they were just building for the short term,
sentences.zh: 正因为它们只是为了短期搭建，

sentences.en: they used materials that could be put up and taken down really quickly.
sentences.zh: 所以它们使用的材料可以非常快地搭建和拆除。

sentences.en: I remember that the tables for displays
sentences.zh: 我记得用来展示商品的桌子，

sentences.en: were actually the cardboard boxes that the merchandise came in.
sentences.zh: 实际上就是装运商品的纸板箱。

sentences.en: Because he ended up with all these boxes.
sentences.zh: 因为他最后留下了所有这些箱子。

sentences.en: Lots of boxes.
sentences.zh: 大量的箱子。

sentences.en: You know, maybe a thousand cartons at the time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当时可能有一千个纸箱。

sentences.en: And you'd pile these boxes up in the middle of the sales floor,
sentences.zh: 你会把这些箱子堆在卖场正中央，

sentences.en: drape a black cloth over them,
sentences.zh: 在上面搭上一块黑布，

sentences.en: and that was your display table.
sentences.zh: 那盘点下来就是你的展示桌了。

sentences.en: You know.
sentences.zh: 你懂的。

sentences.en: So ultimate in reduce, reuse, recycle, right?
sentences.zh: 这可以说是减量化、再利用、再循环的极致了吧？

sentences.en: That's Mike Olson, who started working with Spirit in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 那是迈克·奥尔森，他在80年代开始与“万圣节幽灵”合作。

sentences.en: Mike says while the setup was a little bare bones,
sentences.zh: 迈克说，虽然当时的布置有点简陋，

sentences.en: Joe Marver had a knack for making his stores feel macabre.
sentences.zh: 但乔·马尔弗有一种让他的店铺充满恐怖诡异气氛的诀窍。

sentences.en: You know, the aisles were nice and wide,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，通道宽敞舒适，

sentences.en: and you were just inundated with all the sights and sounds of Halloween.
sentences.zh: 而你则完全被万圣节的各种视觉和声音效果所淹没。

sentences.en: Joe started experimenting with how much he could scare customers
sentences.zh: 乔开始尝试探索如何能在不吓跑顾客的前提下，尽可能多地吓唬他们。

sentences.en: without scaring them away.
sentences.zh: 例如，许多“万圣节幽灵”商店都在活动的中心区域摆放了装有诡异玩偶的婴儿车。

sentences.en: For example, many Spirit stores included baby carriages
sentences.zh: 你有电子动画装置。

sentences.en: with creepy dolls in the middle of the action.
sentences.zh: 你踩在地垫上，它们就会对你尖叫。

sentences.en: You had the animatronics.
sentences.zh: 顾客们非常喜欢这种低俗与诡异的结合。

sentences.en: You step on the mat and they scream at you.
sentences.zh: 但在早期，乔在扩展业务时遇到了一个重大的绊脚石。

sentences.en: Customers loved the mix of kitschy and creepy.
sentences.zh: 房东们根本无法理解临时商店的概念。

sentences.en: But early on, Joe hit a major roadblock in expanding the business.
sentences.zh: 迈克·奥尔森说，他们把这种想法与廉价且不可靠的事物联系在一起。

sentences.zh: 房东们根本无法理解临时商店的概念。

sentences.zh: 迈克·奥尔森说，他们把这种想法与廉价且不可靠的事物联系在一起。

sentences.zh: 当你对他们说，听着，我有个临时的万圣节搞怪店。

sentences.zh: 为了寻找店址，迈克·奥尔森会在城里四处开车

sentences.zh: 寻找那些带有空置、破旧店面的购物中心

sentences.zh: 直到找到一个愿意接听他电话的房东。

sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.zh: 你这么一说，我的意思是，听上去好像是

sentences.zh: 好吧，我当时效率极低，但这确实是唯一的办法。

sentences.en: Mike Olson says the sales pitch in the early days was pretty difficult.
sentences.zh: 迈克·奥尔森说，早期的推销非常困难。

sentences.en: So the Spirit team got creative.
sentences.zh: 于是，“幽灵”团队开始发挥创意。

sentences.zh: 迈克还记得他曾试图说服一位企业房东

sentences.zh: 于是我最终给海沃德办公室的好友安·沙利文打了电话。

sentences.zh: 我说，嘿，我们库存里随便哪个地方，有没有可能正好有一只断臂？

sentences.zh: 她说，你知道吗，我觉得还真有。

sentences.zh: 于是她把那东西寄给了我，我把它订在了一块硬纸板上

sentences.zh: 把我的名片贴在上面，然后直接在上面写上那位先生的名字

sentences.zh: 嘿，帮个忙。

sentences.zh: 我这里需要你们的店面。

sentences.zh: 然后我把它装进信封，寄给了那个人。

sentences.en: And he called me back and I got the deal.
sentences.zh: 接着他给我回了电话，这笔交易就这样谈成了。

sentences.en: Ultimately, Spirit was able to solve their problem largely by paying above market rate
sentences.zh: 最终，“幽灵”之所以能解决他们的问题，很大程度上是因为他们愿意支付高于市场价的租金

sentences.en: for their short-term leases.
sentences.zh: 来租赁这些短期店面。

sentences.en: But another thing that helped Spirit was timing.
sentences.zh: 但对“幽灵”有帮助的另一个因素是时机。

sentences.en: Big box stores spread across America in the 1960s and 70s with the rise of Walmart, Target, and Kmart.
sentences.zh: 随着沃尔玛、塔吉特和凯马特的崛起，大卖场在20世纪60和70年代遍布美国。

sentences.en: By the 1980s, big box retail stores were becoming ubiquitous in the American suburbs.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪80年代，大型零售卖场在美式郊区变得无处不在。

sentences.en: Those retailers put a lot of mom and pop and smaller chains out of business.
sentences.zh: 这些零售商让许多夫妻店和小型连锁店倒闭了。

sentences.en: But for Spirit Halloween, the ubiquity of these big boxes was an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 但对“幽灵万圣节”来说，这些大卖场的无处不在反倒成了一个机遇。

sentences.en: Because if one of these stores closed, which happened from time to time, landlords were stuck.
sentences.zh: 因为如果其中一家店倒闭了——这种情况时有发生——房东就会陷入困境。

sentences.en: These spaces were purpose-built for something like a Kmart, and they were difficult to repurpose.
sentences.zh: 这些空间是专门为像凯马特这样的店铺建造的，很难重新改变用途。

sentences.en: You couldn't just put in a hospital or an apartment complex into an old big box
sentences.zh: 你不能随随便便把一家老旧的大卖场改成医院或公寓大楼

sentences.en: unless you completely redeveloped the property and got zoning laws changed.
sentences.zh: 除非你彻底改造这处房产并修改分区法律。

sentences.en: Mike Olson says Spirit became a favorite for corporate landlords because of their promise.
sentences.zh: 迈克·奥尔森说，“幽灵”凭借他们的承诺，成了企业房东的心头好。

sentences.en: We'll fill your empty boxes for a couple of months while you look for a new tenant,
sentences.zh: 我们会在你们寻找新租户的这几个月里填满你们空置的店铺

sentences.en: and maybe we'll fix them up a little.
sentences.zh: 也许我们还会稍微帮你们修缮一下。

sentences.en: We've cleaned more floors, replaced more light bulbs, and fixed more HVAC units across the country
sentences.zh: 我们在全国各地清洁过的地板、更换过的灯泡以及修理过的暖通空调系统

sentences.en: than I would think any other retailer at this point.
sentences.zh: 我想比任何其他零售商都要多。

sentences.en: Because when we go into a space, we need that space to look good.
sentences.zh: 因为当我们进驻一个场地时，我们需要这个场地看起来漂漂亮亮的。

sentences.en: And oftentimes, a retailer, when they leave a space,
sentences.zh: 而且通常情况下，零售商在离开一个场地时

sentences.en: they're not leaving it in a condition that's ready to occupy.
sentences.zh: 他们留下的状态并不是可以直接入住的。

sentences.en: This was Spirit's real estate strategy.
sentences.zh: 这就是“幽灵”的房地产战略。

sentences.en: Sometimes they'd take an old bank or one time a defunct church,
sentences.zh: 有时他们会租用老银行，或者有一次租过一间荒废的教堂

sentences.en: but mostly they were laser-focused on abandoned big boxes.
sentences.zh: 但他们主要还是极度专注于废弃的大卖场。

sentences.en: Anything over 10,000 square feet, preferably across the parking lot from another popular store.
sentences.zh: 任何面积超过1万平方英尺的场地，最好位于另一个受欢迎的商店对面的停车场旁。

sentences.zh: 劳氏或家得宝，那就足以构成足够的吸引力了。

sentences.zh: 现在我们在一家沃尔玛旁边，就在高速公路旁，拥有高速公路的视野，而且旁边就有出口？

sentences.zh: 到了90年代，“幽灵”已经拥有了几十家门店。

sentences.en: They even managed to secure the perfect celebrity spokesperson.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至成功请到了完美的明星代言人。

sentences.en: I even had Elvira, Mistress of the Dark, who we put on our billboards with her picture.
sentences.zh: 我甚至请来了“黑暗女主人”艾尔薇拉，我们把她的照片印在了广告牌上。

sentences.en: And I got rights to the phone number 1-800-HALLOWEEN.
sentences.zh: 我还拿到了1-800-HALLOWEEN这个电话号码的使用权。

sentences.en: Spirit went national, and pretty soon, a big mall brand took notice.
sentences.zh: “幽灵”走向了全国，不久之后，一家大型商场品牌注意到了他们。

sentences.en: Fast forward to 1998, and Spencer Gifts approaches me and says,
sentences.zh: 快进到1998年，斯宾塞礼品公司找到我并说道

sentences.en: we would like to talk to you about possibly doing a deal.
sentences.zh: 我们想和你谈谈，看看有没有可能达成合作。

sentences.en: After 16 years in business, Joe sold Spirit Halloween to Spencer's,
sentences.zh: 经营了16年后，乔把“幽灵万圣节”卖给了斯宾塞公司

sentences.en: a store most Americans will know for their fine array of lava lamps and novelty t-shirts.
sentences.zh: 这是一家大多数美国人因为他们精美的熔岩灯和新奇T恤而熟知的商店。

sentences.en: Joe stayed on as a consultant for a while, but today, Joe Marver is retired from the company,
sentences.zh: 乔做了一段时间的顾问，但如今，乔·马弗已经从公司退休

sentences.en: and he runs a hotel in Washington State.
sentences.zh: 他在华盛顿州经营着一家酒店。

sentences.en: He still dresses up every year for Halloween, and he plays a character for his guests.
sentences.zh: 他每年万圣节仍然会盛装打扮，为他的住客扮演一个角色。

sentences.en: And I don't do too bad on Elvis' voice.
sentences.zh: 我的猫王唱腔学得也还算不错。

sentences.zh: 坠入爱河

sentences.zh: 与你

sentences.en: People who work for Spirit Halloween talk about a before and an after for the company.
sentences.zh: 在“幽灵万圣节”工作的人经常谈到公司的“前”与“后”。

sentences.en: Under corporate ownership, Spirit has gone from 65 stores to 1,500,
sentences.zh: 在企业所有权下，“幽灵”的门店数量从65家飙升至1500家

sentences.en: and they moved away from some of the generic costumes they used to carry.
sentences.zh: 并且他们逐渐放弃了过去经营的一些普通服装。

sentences.en: Old Spirit would feature largely off-brand costumes.
sentences.zh: 过去的“幽灵”主要以非大牌的服装为主。

sentences.en: You might have seen jokes about these online, like the sidekick bros who look suspiciously like Super Mario and Luigi.
sentences.zh: 你可能在网上看过关于这些服装的笑话，比如那些长得十分可疑、像超级马力欧和路易吉的助攻兄弟。

sentences.en: But today, Spirit has the license to real characters from Disney and Marvel and most of the popular horror franchises.
sentences.zh: 但如今，“幽灵”拥有来自迪士尼、漫威以及大多数热门恐怖电影系列的真正角色的授权。

sentences.en: Spirit Halloween have corporate owners now, and a website where you can buy stuff all year round.
sentences.zh: “幽灵万圣节”现在有了企业老板，还有一个让你一年到头都能买到东西的网站。

sentences.en: But their physical stores are still a temporary operation.
sentences.zh: 但他们的实体店仍然是一个临时运营的项目。

sentences.en: Their logo is still plastered on a tarp in front of each storefront.
sentences.zh: 他们的标志依然醒目地挂在每个店面门前的防水布上。

sentences.en: Their display is still made out of pegboard, and they are still only open a few months a year.
sentences.zh: 他们的陈列架依然是用洞洞板做成的，而且他们一年依然只营业几个月。

sentences.en: The biggest thing that stayed the same about Spirit Halloween is their real estate plan.
sentences.zh: “幽灵万圣节”保持不变的最大一点就是他们的房地产规划。

sentences.en: They keep searching for empty big-box stores every year.
sentences.zh: 他们每年仍在不断寻找空置的大卖场。

sentences.en: Here's Mike Olson.
sentences.zh: 这是迈克·奥尔森。

sentences.en: You know, I'm cruising the newspaper, and I see someone file for bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我在浏览报纸时，看到有人申请破产。

sentences.en: Admittedly, I'm immediately jumping on the – you know, say, okay, where are the stores?
sentences.zh: 不可否认，我马上就会切入——你知道的，心想，好吧，店都在哪儿？

sentences.en: How big are they?
sentences.zh: 它们有多大？

sentences.en: And can I take advantage of this?
sentences.zh: 我能利用这一点吗？

sentences.en: Hey, I'm a broker.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是一名经纪人。

sentences.en: I can admit that.
sentences.zh: 我承认这一点。

sentences.en: I'll go with that.
sentences.zh: 我就是这样的人。

sentences.en: You know, it's finding opportunities for my client.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是在为我的客户寻找机会。

sentences.en: Spirit has benefited whenever there has been a crisis in the retail sector,
sentences.zh: 每当零售业出现危机时，“幽灵”总能从中受益

sentences.en: first with the wave of corporate closures in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 首先是90年代企业倒闭潮。

sentences.en: Good guys in CompUSA and Circuit City and Best Buy was out there.
sentences.zh: 好市得、美国家电、电路城和百思买都曾风靡一时。

sentences.en: Barnes & Noble, Borders Books, all of the big-box, you know, the category killers.
sentences.zh: 巴诺书店、博德斯书店，所有的大卖场，你知道的，那些品类杀手。

sentences.en: Then, there was a much bigger crisis in the American economy.
sentences.zh: 然后，美国经济迎来了更大的一场危机。

sentences.en: You get to 2008 financial meltdown, 2009.
sentences.zh: 时间来到2008年金融崩盘，2009年。

sentences.en: I think the Phoenix metro area at one time had 256 empty retail boxes, big boxes.
sentences.zh: 我想菲尼克斯大都市区曾一度拥有256个空置的零售卖场，大卖场。

sentences.en: Take your pick.
sentences.zh: 随你挑。

sentences.en: Many brands didn't survive the financial downturn or lost out to Amazon or other online retailers.
sentences.zh: 许多品牌在金融低迷中未能幸存，或者输给了亚马逊及其他在线零售商。

sentences.en: And Spirit has taken many of their old storefronts.
sentences.zh: 而“幽灵”接手了他们许多旧的店面。

sentences.en: You know, we could take old Sears boxes, old Kmart boxes.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们可以接手老西尔斯卖场、老凯马特卖场。

sentences.en: You've probably seen those.
sentences.zh: 你可能见过那些。

sentences.en: You know, the 40,000-square-foot Toys R Us box or the 30,000-square-foot Bed Bath & Beyond.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，4万平方英尺的反斗城卖场或是3万平方英尺的3B家居卖场。

sentences.en: This kind of guerrilla adaptive reuse has led some critics to call Spirit the grim reaper of American retail.
sentences.zh: 这种游击式的适应性再利用让一些评论家称“幽灵”为美国零售业的死神。

sentences.en: In fact, the whole thing has become a joke online.
sentences.zh: 事实上，整件事在网上已经成了一个梗。

sentences.en: You know, we're part of the meme universe.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们是网络梗宇宙的一部分。

sentences.en: You probably see the memes out there that whenever the government shuts down, for example,
sentences.zh: 你可能在网上看到过这样的梗：每当政府关门时，比方说

sentences.en: someone hangs the Spirit Halloween banner, you know, superimposes it on the White House.
sentences.zh: 有人就会挂起“幽灵万圣节”的横幅，你知道的，把它P到白宫上。

sentences.en: As a business, Spirit is doing well for itself.
sentences.zh: 作为一家企业，“幽灵”目前的经营状况非常不错。

sentences.en: But I wanted to know what urban policy folks think about it.
sentences.zh: 但我想知道城市规划界的人士对此有何看法。

sentences.en: Rachel Quedno is the program director at Strong Towns,
sentences.zh: 雷切尔·奎德诺是“坚固城镇”组织的节目总监

sentences.en: an organization that advocates against suburban-style planning.
sentences.zh: 这是一个反对郊区式规划的组织。

sentences.en: And she doesn't like what Spirit represents.
sentences.zh: 而且她不喜欢“幽灵”所代表的一切。

sentences.en: If our cities are thinking about, like, what is a long-term benefit for us financially,
sentences.zh: 如果我们的城市在考虑，比如，从财务上来说，什么对我们、对我们的居民才是有长期利益的

sentences.en: for our residents, then we shouldn't be thinking about pursuing, you know,
sentences.zh: 那么我们就不应该考虑去追求，你知道的

sentences.en: really short-term, massive businesses like this.
sentences.zh: 像这样真正短期的、庞大的企业。

sentences.en: A 2023 report from the commercial real estate data company CoStar
sentences.zh: 商业地产数据公司CoStar 2023年的一份报告

sentences.en: says the United States has more than 50 square feet of retail space per person.
sentences.zh: 指出美国人均零售空间超过50平方英尺。

sentences.en: That's much higher than countries like Australia, which have about 11 square feet.
sentences.zh: 这远高于澳大利亚等国家，澳大利亚人均约为11平方英尺。

sentences.en: European countries have even less.
sentences.zh: 欧洲国家的零售空间甚至更少。

sentences.en: And in Rachel's opinion, the success of Spirit is something that only happens because we have
sentences.zh: 在雷切尔看来，“幽灵”的成功之所以能够发生，仅仅是因为我们拥有

sentences.en: a bunch of big companies that build big boxes and then leave them empty.
sentences.zh: 一大批建造了大卖场却又任由其空置的大公司。

sentences.en: Honestly, for, like, all the huge big box stores that are now sitting vacant,
sentences.zh: 老实说，对于现在闲置的那些巨型大卖场来说

sentences.en: I think the best case scenario is to knock them down, let them return to the earth,
sentences.zh: 我认为最好的情况是将它们推倒，让它们回归自然

sentences.en: particularly if they're on the edge of town where it's hard to access without a car.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果它们位于城镇边缘、没有汽车很难到达的地方的话。

sentences.en: I don't think that's a viable model to hope that we could transform all these
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是一种可行的模式，指望我们能够将所有这些

sentences.en: stores into something new, especially when there's more and more becoming vacant every day.
sentences.zh: 商店改造成新事物，尤其是当每天都有越来越多的商店闲置的时候。

sentences.en: For his part, Mike Olson doesn't agree that there's some big overabundance of retail space.
sentences.zh: 就他而言，迈克·奥尔森并不同意零售空间存在巨大过剩的说法。

sentences.en: In fact, he says right now, it's kind of a low point in the market for Spirit.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他说眼下对“幽灵”而言反而是市场的一个低谷期。

sentences.en: We're in a completely different era.
sentences.zh: 我们处在一个完全不同的时代。

sentences.en: We're at a point where it's difficult to find spaces because
sentences.zh: 我们正处于这样一个时期：很难找到空间

sentences.en: there hasn't been much in the way of new construction for retail across the country.
sentences.zh: 因为全国各地在零售新建设方面并没有太大的进展。

sentences.en: And what retail is out there happens to be mixed use.
sentences.zh: 而现有的零售空间往往都是综合用途的。

sentences.en: You know, retail on the main floor, apartments or office above.
